Diplomat Lana Nusseibeh has
[entered](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/25/lana-nusseibeh-
emirati-diplomat-enters-un-secretary-general-race) the race to succeed Antonio
Guterres as the United Nations' 10th Secretary-General. If she succeeds, she
will be the first woman, the first Muslim, and the first person of Palestinian
descent to be appointed UN Secretary-General.

She sounds great, right?

_Wrong._

Nusseibeh was [until earlier this
month](https://www.un.org/sg/sites/default/files/document/2026-10/cv-lana-
nusseibeh.pdf) minister of state in the Emirati foreign ministry, and spent
much of the past decade as the United Arab Emirates' Permanent Representative
to the United Nations. In both positions, she has whitewashed the UAE's
involvement in the genocide in Sudan. She might have - for want of a better
phrase - _gallons_ of blood on her hands.

If the UN Security Council confirms Nusseibeh as the next secretary-general -
and her chances are pretty high, given that all of the other candidates are
[believed to be opposed](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/uae-
nominates-diplomat-lana-nusseibeh-as-un-secretary-general-potentially-
breaking-deadlock/) by the Trump administration - it will be making a
monumental error of judgment, which could destroy the [already weakened
credibility](https://www.wsj.com/world/world-leaders-almost-all-agree-on-one-
thing-the-u-n-is-failing-8740b01d) of the UN for generations to come.

First, some background on what has been
[repeatedly](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/after-3-years-of-relentless-
war-sudan-faces-worlds-worst-humanitarian-crisis)
[described](https://www.who.int/news/item/09-01-2026-sudan-1000-days-of-war-
deepen-the-world-s-worst-health-and-humanitarian-crisis) as ["the world's
worst humanitarian crisis."](https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/08/1168188)
